principle: Face direction is style-dependent. Facial realism and skin texture support refined makeup and visual appeal while preserving identity and apparent age; maximum texture is not the objective.

beauty_first.label: Beauty-First Face
beauty_first.goal: preserve youthful attractiveness, elegance and character appeal before increasing facial realism
prompt_translation: Preserve a youthful, elegant and beautiful face as the highest facial priority.
Keep soft cheek tissue, a refined oval facial read and clear youthful eyes; do not age the character up in order to make the face more realistic.
Build facial realism on refined makeup: delicate skin response, natural lips and brows, restrained eye definition and soft facial volume; keep texture subordinate to the finished face and framing.
Put stronger realism into hair, body, hands, costume materials and lighting rather than forcing the face toward a mature fashion-model look.

humanized_real.label: Humanized Real Face
humanized_real.goal: increase photographic human presence while preserving identity and attractiveness
prompt_translation: Increase realistic human presence in the face while preserving the approved identity and attractiveness.

Establish refined makeup first; believable eyelids, soft tissue, restrained regional skin response and natural nose/lip structure should support an attractive finish rather than compete with it. Scale texture to framing without coarse sharpening or plastic smoothing.
Keep the face young and attractive; realism must not become fatigue, hollowness or age inflation.

stylized_beauty.label: Stylized Beauty Face
stylized_beauty.goal: preserve idealized visual appeal and stylized facial design with only minimal realism pressure
prompt_translation: Preserve the stylized beauty design and idealized facial appeal.
Use only minimal skin realism and keep the face polished, youthful and intentionally stylized.
Apply stronger realism to materials, body, hands, hair physics and lighting without forcing the face into photographic realism.
